metaTitle: Court Fee & Stamp Refund Rules in Bangladesh
title: Court Fee & Stamp Refund Rules in Bangladesh
metaDescription: Claim a refund for spoiled non-judicial stamps or excess court fees in Bangladesh under the Stamp Act 1899 & Court-Fees Act 1870. Learn deadlines & steps.
keywords: unused judicial stamp refund DC office
heroIntro: Under Sections 49 to 55 of the Stamp Act, 1899 and Sections 13 to 15 of the Court-Fees Act, 1870, litigants and property buyers in Bangladesh can claim a refund for spoiled, unused, or excess non-judicial stamp paper and court fees. Applications for spoiled stamp refunds must generally be filed before the District Collector (DC Office) within 6 months.

quickAnswer.heading: At a Glance: Court Fee & Stamp Refunds
points: Governing Laws: Stamp Act, 1899 (Sections 49–55) & Court-Fees Act, 1870 (Sections 13, 14 & 15).
Stamp Refund Deadline: Within 6 months from the date the stamp was spoiled or became useless (Section 50, Stamp Act 1899).
Court Fee Refund Grounds: Appellate remand (Sec. 13), review admission (Sec. 14–15), or excess payment by court mistake.
Deduction: Standard statutory treasury deduction (typically 10% under Stamp Act rules) applies to cash refunds.

sections.h2: When You Can Claim a Court Fee Refund Under the Court-Fees Act, 1870
sections.content:
Sections 13, 14, and 15 of the Court-Fees Act, 1870 empower civil and appellate courts to issue a refund certificate authorising the District Collector to reimburse court fees paid in specific statutory circumstances. Under Section 13, if a suit is dismissed on a preliminary point and the appellate court reverses the order and remands the case for fresh trial, the appellant is entitled to a certificate for the full court fee paid on the memorandum of appeal.

Similarly, under Section 14 and Section 15, if an application for review of judgment is admitted on grounds of mistake or error apparent on the face of the record, or if a court reverses its former decision, the applicant receives a refund certificate for the excess fee paid above the review threshold. Courts also exercise inherent jurisdiction under Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 to refund excess fees paid due to bona fide miscalculation or when a plaint is returned for lack of jurisdiction.

For litigants appealing civil or commercial orders, review our appeal, review, and revision guide or consult a Supreme Court lawyer in Bangladesh.

sections.h2: Spoiled and Unused Non-Judicial Stamp Refunds Under the Stamp Act, 1899
sections.content:
Section 49 of the Stamp Act, 1899 allows the District Collector to refund or exchange non-judicial stamp paper that was spoiled before execution, written on by mistake, or rendered useless because a party refused to sign or a land transaction fell through. Likewise, Section 54 permits refunds for stamps purchased in good faith that are no longer needed, provided they are clean, unexecuted, and presented within the statutory window.

This is particularly valuable in high-value Dhaka property transactions where buyers purchase tens of thousands of taka in non-judicial stamps for a land sale deed or Power of Attorney, only for the seller to back out before registration at the Sub-Registry Office.

However, if a deed has already been signed and registered, the Stamp Act does not refund stamp duty simply because the parties later cancel the contract. Always verify seller title via online khatian checks before buying high-value stamp paper.

sections.h2: Statutory Deadlines and Deductions at the DC Treasury
sections.content:
Missing the strict limitation window under Section 50 of the Stamp Act, 1899 forfeits your right to a cash refund or replacement stamps, so track the purchase and cancellation dates carefully.

Refund TypeGoverning ProvisionFiling DeadlineDeduction / Outcome
Spoiled Unexecuted StampSection 49 & 50(1), Stamp Act 18996 months from date of spoilingCash refund minus statutory deduction (approx. 10%) or fresh stamps.
Unused Clean StampSection 54, Stamp Act 18996 months from date of purchaseCash refund minus 10% deduction upon vendor receipt verification.
Court Fee on Remand / ReviewSections 13–15, Court-Fees Act 1870Within appeal/review disposal100% refund certificate issued by court to DC Treasury.
Excess / Erroneous Court FeeSection 151 CPC, 1908Promptly upon court orderRefund of excess portion via DC Treasury bill.

Note that while e-stamp and pay-order fees used in modern Sub-Registry offices follow parallel Bangladesh Bank / Treasury refund circulars, the 6-month Stamp Act principle still guides verification.

sections.h2: Step-by-Step Procedure to Obtain Your Refund
sections.content:
Follow these five steps to convert a court refund certificate or spoiled stamp paper into a treasury disbursement:

  1. Secure the Court Certificate or Vendor Receipt: For court fees, file a petition under Sections 13–15 of the Court-Fees Act, 1870 asking the presiding judge to sign a Refund Certificate. For non-judicial stamps, keep the licensed stamp vendor's original purchase slip.
  2. Submit Application to the District Collector (DC Office): File a formal refund petition before the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) or Treasury Officer within 6 months under Section 50 of the Stamp Act, 1899.
  3. Treasury & Forensic Verification: The DC Stamp Branch verifies the serial numbers, watermarks, and vendor register to confirm the stamps are genuine and unexecuted.
  4. Sanction Order & Deduction Calculation: Upon verification, the Collector issues a sanction order deducting the statutory percentage (typically 10% for cash refunds under Section 53).
  5. Collect Payment via Pay Order / Treasury Cheque: Submit the sanction bill at the District Accounts / Treasury Office to receive the reimbursed amount. For complex commercial disputes, consult Advocate Md. Shah Alam or review contract breach remedies.

sections.h2: Documents Checklist for Stamp and Court Fee Refunds
sections.content:
Attach these original records when submitting your refund file to the court or DC Stamp Branch:

  • Original spoiled or unused non-judicial stamp papers (intact, with serial numbers and vendor endorsement visible).
  • Original stamped purchase receipt from the licensed stamp vendor or Sonali Bank Treasury Challan copy.
  • Certified copy of the court order and original Court Fee Refund Certificate (for Sections 13–15 claims).
  • Affidavit explaining why the stamp became spoiled or unused (e.g., cancelled property deal) and confirming no double claim.
  • Applicant's National ID (NID) copy and Power of Attorney if filed through a representative or advocate.

If your refund relates to a cancelled property deal or corporate filing, explore our RJSC corporate filing guide or book a free initial consultation with our chamber.

faqs.question: Can I get a refund if a court case is settled out of court through compromise?
faqs.answer: Under the Court-Fees Act, 1870, voluntary compromise (Solenama) does not automatically grant a statutory refund under Sections 13–15 unless covered by specific mediation or Lok Adalat rules. However, you can petition the court under Section 151 CPC if the suit was withdrawn before framing of issues.

faqs.question: What is the time limit to apply for a spoiled stamp paper refund in Bangladesh?
faqs.answer: Under Section 50 of the Stamp Act, 1899, you must apply to the District Collector within 6 months from the date the stamp was spoiled or became useless. Applications filed after 6 months are generally barred.

faqs.question: Does the government deduct any fee from a stamp paper refund?
faqs.answer: Yes. Under Section 53 of the Stamp Act, 1899, when the Collector issues a cash refund for spoiled or unused stamps rather than exchanging them for fresh stamps, a statutory deduction (typically 10% per taka) is withheld.

faqs.question: Can I claim a refund if I lost the stamp vendor's receipt?
faqs.answer: While the vendor's receipt speeds up verification, the DC Stamp Branch can still verify the stamp's authenticity using the serial number and the licensed vendor's bound sale register, supported by your sworn affidavit.

faqs.question: Are e-challan or pay-order stamp duty deposits refundable if a land sale cancels?
faqs.answer: Yes. If a land registration is cancelled before deed execution at the Sub-Registry Office, the buyer can apply to the Sub-Registrar for a non-utilisation certificate and submit it to the District Treasury or Bangladesh Bank for a refund.
